title: Lexicographically Largest String After Pair Transformations
summary: Given an integer array nums, for each integer x in nums, start with a string consisting of exactly x lowercase 'a' characters.
statement: Given an integer array nums, for each integer x in nums, start with a string consisting of exactly x lowercase 'a' characters. You can perform the following operation any number of times (including zero times): - Choose two adjacent equal letters in the string and replace them with the next letter in the alphabet. For example, "aa" can be replaced with "b", and "bb" can be replaced with "c". The pair "zz" cannot be replaced. Determine the lexicographically largest string that can be obtained for each x. Return an array of strings where the i-th string corresponds to the i-th integer in the input array nums. A string a is considered lexicographically larger than string b if, at the first position where they differ, a contains a letter that appears later in the alphabet than the corresponding letter in b. If the first min(a.length, b.length) characters are equal, the longer string is lexicographically larger.
constraints: Each positive x begins as x copies of a.
Two adjacent equal letters below z may merge into one next letter.
Return the lexicographically largest reachable string for every x.
hints: Merging equal letters is binary carrying: two level-j letters become one level-(j+1) letter.
The final multiset is the set bits of x, and descending letters maximize lexicographic order.
Scan bits high to low and append the corresponding letter for each set bit.
Any unmerged equal pair can be replaced by a larger leading possibility, so the fully carried descending representation is maximal.
editorial: Any unmerged equal pair can be replaced by a larger leading possibility, so the fully carried descending representation is maximal.

tests.explanation: Binary decompositions yield b, ca, and cba.
Powers of two merge completely into a, c, and d respectively.
